passage:
At his new school in Johannesburg, Siddiq began copying how the football crowd talked, dropping his mother's language on the phone, wearing the same low-slung jeans and laughing at jokes he didn't get. On Friday he skipped chess club, because it wasn't cool.
Thabo caught up with him at the gate. "You're doing an impression of somebody."
Siddiq shrugged, then admitted it. "I just want them to like me."
"Fine. Wear the jeans, learn the slang. But I liked you when you were explaining the Sicilian defence."
That weekend Siddiq still hung out with the football group, but he brought a chess board along, and wore what he wanted. Two boys asked to play.

qa.q: Which club did Siddiq skip on Friday?
How did Siddiq feel at his new school, and what did he do about it?
qa.a: He felt insecure and anxious to be liked, admitting "I just want them to like me", so he copied the football crowd's talk and clothes.

qa.q: How did Siddiq balance fitting in with staying himself?
qa.a: He kept some of the group's style but brought his chess board and wore what he wanted, so he adapted lightly and kept his core.

qa.q: How does Thabo see Siddiq's change?
qa.a: Thabo sees a friend doing an impression of somebody else, and reminds him that he was liked for who he was, chess included.

grounding: Shows a teen changing his talk and dress to fit in, and Thabo helping him keep his core.
